newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron gunman sent to pyschiatric hospital.
newsitem.headline: Hebron gunman sent to pyschiatric hospital.

text.p: An Israeli military court decided on Thursday that a soldier who shot and wounded seven Palestinians in Hebron last month was unfit to stand trial and must be confined to a psychiatric hospital, the army said.

Noam Friedman, a 22-year-old conscript, told the court he shot into a crowd of Arabs in a Hebron marketplace on New Year's Day to prevent Israel from handing over most of the town to Palestinian self-rule.

Friedman also said he wanted to avenge the death of Baruch Goldstein, a Jewish settler who massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in a Hebron mosque three years ago this week. Goldstein was beaten to death by survivors.
An army spokesman said that before the start of a trial, a military court in Jaffa asked a team of psychiatrists to examine Friedman.
"In accordance with the psychiatrists' findings, the court ordered Friedman sent to a psychiatric hospital and therefore no charges will be filed against him," an army spokesman said.
He said it had not yet been determined for how long Friedman would be confined to the facility.

The Itim news agency reported the psychiatrists found that Friedman, a religious Jew who lives in a West Bank settlement, was schizophrenic and the army had begun an investigation into how he had been conscripted.
An Israeli officer overpowered Friedman shortly after he opened fire from his M-16 automatic rifle.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule on January 17 under a peace deal.
